fields.Name: SS Edmund Fitzgerald
fields.Namesake: Named for Edmund Fitzgerald, chairman of Northwestern Mutual
fields.Operator: Columbia Transportation Division, Oglebay Norton Company of Cleveland, Ohio
fields.Builder: Great Lakes Engineering Works of River Rouge, Michigan
fields.Nickname(s): Fitz, Mighty Fitz, Big Fitz, Pride of the American Side, Toledo Express, Titanic of the Great Lakes
fields.Fate: Lost with all hands (29 crew) in a storm, November 10, 1975
fields.Length: 729 ft (222 m) overall [ 4 ] 711 ft (217 m) between perpendiculars [ 4 ]
fields.Installed power: As built: Coal fired Westinghouse Electric Corporation steam turbine at 7,500 shp (5,600 kW) After refit: Conversion to oil fuel and the fitting of automated boiler controls over the winter of 1971–72. Carried 72,000 U.S. gal (270,000 L; 60,000 imp gal) fuel oil
fields.Propulsion: Single fixed pitch 19.5 ft (5.9 m) propeller
